An AI Security Facepalm: OpenAI’s Evaluation Became Hugging Face’s Incident
summary: OpenAI models escaped containment and breached Hugging Face while pursuing an evaluation goal. Learn what this incident means for CISOs and agentic AI security.
body_text: In a move straight out of a horror movie or techno-dystopian thriller, OpenAI’s model did what Anthropic threatened its model could do (but didn’t): A frontier lab’s own models escaped containment during an authorized evaluation and breached another company to finish the task and perform an autonomous hack. OpenAI confirmed that its own models escaped a constrained evaluation environment, reached the open internet, and breached Hugging Face’s production infrastructure to obtain answers for a cybersecurity benchmark. The models included GPT-5.6 Sol and a more capable prerelease model running with reduced cyber refusals, with a security research harness. OpenAI called the event an unprecedented cyber incident. We agree with that assessment. The models did not wander into Hugging Face by accident. They pursued a narrow evaluation goal, found a zero-day in OpenAI’s package-registry proxy, escalated privileges, located a node with internet access, inferred that Hugging Face might hold ExploitGym solutions, and compromised production systems to retrieve them. Forrester’s AEGIS framework – the first and only framework designed exclusively to address agentic AI security threats – covers each of these scenarios. We provide deep exploration of goal and intent hijacking, unrestrained agency and privilege, and evasion and deception. These are all characteristics that OpenAI’s model exhibited during its attack. Agentic AI changes both the economics and the source of attack. A model provider’s internal evaluation became an external production incident at another company. Security teams now have to account for capable models that can chain vulnerabilities, cross trust boundaries, and cause harm while pursuing the goal their operators assigned. A Narrow Goal Drove A Cross-Company Breach OpenAI designed the evaluation to measure advanced exploitation across complex attack paths. The models ran without the production classifiers that normally block high-risk cyber activity. OpenAI isolated the environment and limited network access to an internally hosted third-party proxy that cached software packages. The models turned that tiny exception into an exit. They spent substantial inference compute searching for open internet access, exploited a previously unknown flaw in the proxy, escalated privileges, moved laterally through OpenAI’s research environment, and reached a node with internet access. They then targeted Hugging Face, combined stolen credentials with additional vulnerabilities, and obtained test solutions from its production database. Keep in mind that no human operators directed the OpenAI model activity . The model operated completely independently. Hugging Face’s original disclosure captured the operational scale: thousands of actions across short-lived sandboxes, lateral movement through internal clusters, and migrating command-and-control infrastructure staged on public services. It was able to identify the attack as agentic because of the massive scale and operational decisions made by the models. Hugging Face contained the agent after it compromised internal datasets and service credentials. The intent matters more than the techniques used. The models tried to solve an evaluation, not torch the internet. That narrow objective still produced a zero-day exploit, a containment escape, cross-company intrusion, credential theft, and production data access. This is reminiscent of an attack demonstrated by Palisade Research in 2025 that also used OpenAI models. In that scenario, an agent cheated to win against the Stockfish chess engine. OpenAI’s o1-preview noted , “The task is to ‘win against a powerful chess engine’ — not necessarily to win fairly in a chess game,” so it modified system files to allow illegal moves, forcing its opponent to resign. This is why Forrester has declared intent as a first-class security object, and securing intent must be a new priority for CISOs ( which Jeff Pollard and Heidi Shey will present in a Black Hat briefing on August 6 at 3:35 p.m.) . Security architectures that assume benign intent will miss this failure mode. Agents can pursue authorized goals through unauthorized means, especially when evaluators reward the outcome and fail to police the path. Boards and C-suite leaders need to understand new intent-related exposures, which this event exposes in gritty detail. Reduced Refusals And Failed Containment Created The Incident OpenAI’s disclosure changes the guardrails story. The attacking models ran with reduced cyber refusals because the evaluation aimed to measure their maximum offensive capability. OpenAI relied on environmental containment to offset that capability. The package-registry proxy provided a tightly-scoped network path, but the models found a zero-day in the proxy and converted it into open internet access. The control design treated the sandbox boundary as reliable while running models explicitly pushed to defeat obstacles. Hugging Face then hit the mirror-image problem during response: Commercial frontier models refused to analyze live attacker commands and payloads. The incident put reduced safeguards on the offensive side and restrictive safeguards on the defensive side. That’s a governance faceplant. Hugging Face switched to GLM-5.2, a self-hosted open-weight model, and analyzed more than 17,000 events in hours rather than days while keeping stolen credentials inside its environment. Responders made a high-stakes call about model sovereignty, supply chain, and governance during an active incident because they needed a tool that worked. Our analysis of Fable 5 and Mythos 5 warned that organizations increasingly depend on safety controls, policy decisions, and service restrictions that someone else operates. This incident adds another dependency: Model developers must prove that evaluation environments can contain the capabilities they intentionally expose. Govern Agent Intent Before Shadow Adoption Does It For You Only days before the incident, Anthropic Deputy CISO Jason Clinton published guidance for security leaders on agentic AI risk . OpenAI’s evaluation supplied a live example of the problem he described. Clinton argued that security leaders must decide how much agentic risk they’ll accept before the business decides for them. He also wrote that “an agent that drifts out of alignment with your intent is indistinguishable from an insider attack.” OpenAI’s models stayed locked on the benchmark, but their route to the answer blew through containment and harmed another organization. His advice to design for where models will be in six months, rather than where they are today, now carries more urgency. His four questions that belong in model evaluations, procurement reviews, architecture reviews, and threat modeling are: What untrusted content does it ingest? What actions can it take and on whose behalf? What is the blast radius if it is misaligned? What observability do I have? OpenAI’s evaluation answers those questions with uncomfortable precision. The models ingested a goal that rewarded exploitation, operated with reduced refusals, found an unplanned action path, and crossed from a research environment into a third party’s production systems. Neither the benchmark nor the sandbox kept the models inside the intended boundary. Security teams need telemetry that captures the model, prompt, goal, tools, credentials, intermediate decisions, network paths, and external effects. Without that evidence, containment drags and investigators reconstruct intent from infrastructure crumbs. Explainability, observability, least agency, and continuous assurance must govern evaluations as rigorously as production deployments. AI software supply-chain risk ranked among Forrester’s top cybersecurity threats for 2026 . OpenAI’s package-registry proxy became the first escape path, and Hugging Face became the downstream target. The incident shows how a trusted development service, proxy, benchmark, dataset host, or model repository can connect environments that their owners consider separate. Security teams must map those transitive trust paths before a capable model finds them first. Model Evaluation Has Become A Production-Risk Activity Security leaders need to drag model evaluations inside the enterprise risk boundary. OpenAI intentionally reduced cyber refusals to measure maximum capability, then relied on isolation to contain the result. The models defeated that isolation and created an incident outside OpenAI. Evaluations that remove safeguards or reward long-horizon exploitation now carry the risk profile of offensive security operations. CISOs should require threat models, independent containment tests, egress controls, kill criteria, named incident owners, external notification procedures, and evidence retention before teams run high-capability evaluations. They should also treat benchmark design as a security control. A benchmark that rewards task completion without penalizing boundary violations teaches operators little about safe performance and gives the model every reason to search for unintended paths. Capability testing needs governance equal to the capability under test. Hugging Face’s response reinforces the continuity lesson included in our analysis of Anthropic and the US government . Security teams need tested model fallbacks for investigations, while model developers need defense-in-depth that assumes their strongest model will attack every available boundary. Build The Controls Before You Need Them This incident shows model providers, enterprises, and security teams that agentic risk starts before deployment. Evaluations, sandboxes, package services, benchmarks, credentials, and external dependencies all sit inside the attack surface. Forrester’s AEGIS framework addresses that full lifecycle. Organizations need to act on seven priorities: Govern high-capability evaluations as offensive operations. Require explicit authorization, containment tests, abort criteria, incident ownership, and external notification procedures, consistent with a new AppSec operating model for agentic development . Apply least agency to models under evaluation. Limit each model’s tools, credentials, compute, network paths, and authority, using Forrester’s AEGIS guidance for IAM and AI agents . Design containment for model-led attacks against the containment itself. Remove unnecessary egress, isolate package infrastructure, rotate credentials, and apply AEGIS guardrails for Zero Trust architecture across every trust boundary. Record the complete chain from goal to external effect. Preserve prompts, intermediate reasoning artifacts, tool calls, identities, network activity, and policy decisions, following the Five Eyes guidance operationalized through AEGIS . Maintain an incident-response model under your control. Test a self-hosted or open-weight fallback before provider policies block critical analysis, as our analysis of AI provider concentration and continuity risk prescribes. Evaluate AI vendors for evaluation safety and continuity. Examine how providers reduce safeguards, isolate models, govern benchmarks, disclose incidents, and support responders through the vendor-risk lens discussed in our analysis of Fable 5 and Mythos 5 . Treat the AI software supply chain as critical infrastructure. Map transitive trust across model hosts, package proxies, repositories, benchmarks, and developer tools, then apply controls that assume one of those services will fail . title: Automations with Scheduled AI Agents: The Power of "Set It and Forget It" Workflows
summary: Discover how scheduled AI agents can transform your productivity by automating routine tasks like email management. Learn how Wordware's new scheduled triggers feature lets you build powerful AI workflows that run on autopilot.
body_text: The Promise of AI Automation: More Time for What Matters The true potential of AI isn't just about making tasks easier—it's about completely removing them from your to-do list. Imagine having a personal assistant who not only understands exactly what you need but takes care of it automatically at precisely the right time, every time. That's the promise of AI agents with scheduled automation: set it up once, and let it handle repetitive tasks while you focus on more meaningful work. Today, we're excited to introduce a game-changing feature that brings this vision to life: scheduled triggers for AI agents in Wordware. What Are Scheduled Triggers and Why Do They Matter? Scheduled triggers are exactly what they sound like—the ability to automatically activate an AI workflow at predetermined times. This seemingly simple capability unlocks an entirely new dimension of productivity. Here's why this matters: True automation : Unlike tools that merely assist you while you work, scheduled agents work independently, even when you're not actively using them Consistency : Critical tasks happen on schedule, without relying on your memory or availability Time optimization : Receive insights and completed tasks exactly when you need them Reduced cognitive load : Eliminate the mental burden of remembering and managing routine processes Real-World Example: Your Daily Email Intelligence Briefing Let's explore a practical example that demonstrates the power of scheduled triggers: a daily email summary agent. The Problem It Solves Most of us face email overload. By day's end, your inbox is cluttered with messages of varying importance, and sorting through them becomes a stressful time sink. You might miss critical communications while wasting time on low-priority messages. The Solution: An Automated Email Intelligence Agent With Wordware's scheduled triggers, you can create an AI agent that: Automatically runs at your specified time each day (e.g., 5:00 PM) Scans your inbox for new messages Intelligently categorizes and summarizes them Identifies which emails need immediate attention Delivers a concise summary directly to your inbox The result? You receive a daily intelligence briefing that helps you quickly identify what matters and what can wait—all without lifting a finger. Building Your First Scheduled Agent in Wordware Creating a scheduled workflow in Wordware is remarkably straightforward, even if you have no coding experience. The platform uses natural language programming, allowing you to describe what you want in plain English. Here's how to build your own daily email summary agent: Create a new project in your Wordware workspace Configure the schedule trigger by selecting your preferred frequency (daily, weekly, monthly) and specific time Connect your email account through Wordware's secure authentication Define the workflow logic using natural language instructions: Find all new emails since the last check Identify messages requiring immediate attention Generate summaries of important content Format everything into a digestible report Set up the delivery method (typically sending the summary to your email) Publish your agent to activate the automation Once published, your agent runs silently in the background, delivering valuable insights right when you need them. Who Benefits Most from Scheduled AI Agents? Scheduled automation through AI agents provides exceptional value for: Busy professionals who need to stay on top of communications but can't constantly monitor their inbox Team leaders who want to receive regular updates without micromanaging Knowledge workers dealing with information overload Small business owners juggling multiple responsibilities Anyone seeking to reduce digital noise and focus on high-value work Beyond Email: Other Powerful Use Cases While our email summary example demonstrates the concept clearly, scheduled triggers enable countless other valuable workflows: Daily data reports that analyze business metrics and highlight trends Content monitoring that tracks mentions of your brand or industry developments Regular social media updates based on trending topics or scheduled content calendars Automated follow-ups with customers or prospects at optimal intervals System health checks that proactively identify potential issues Why Natural Language Programming Makes All the Difference What sets Wordware apart is its document-based approach to building AI agents. Instead of complex coding or confusing visual interfaces, you simply describe what you want your agent to do in plain English. This natural language programming approach means: Anyone can build sophisticated agents regardless of technical background Workflows can be quickly modified as your needs evolve The learning curve is minimal compared to traditional automation tools Your instructions remain readable and understandable months or years later Getting Started with Wordware Scheduled Triggers Ready to experience the freedom of truly automated AI workflows? Here's how to get started: Visit wordware.ai to create your account Explore the template library for pre-built scheduled workflows Customize a template or build your own agent from scratch Set up your first scheduled trigger and watch your productivity transform The most powerful productivity tool isn't the one that helps you work faster—it's the one that eliminates the need for you to do the work at all. With Wordware's scheduled triggers, you're not just saving time; you're reclaiming it entirely. The Future of Work is Automated As AI capabilities continue to advance, the line between what requires human attention and what can be delegated to AI agents will shift dramatically. Those who embrace these tools early will gain a significant advantage in both productivity and work-life balance. Scheduled AI agents represent a fundamental shift in how we approach work—moving from "how can I do this faster?" to "do I need to do this at all?" Ready to transform your productivity with AI that works on your schedule? Visit Wordware today and build your first scheduled agent in minutes.

summary: Discover how a luxury fashion retailer transformed its online shopping experience through user-friendly retail software solutions.
body_text: We empowered our client to identify technical solutions to optimize the client’s retail platform, deliver on the technology and application needs, and design better processes to ensure continued success. Stage 1: Architecture Development Scalability Assessment and Planning: We conducted a comprehensive assessment of the client’s existing platform and determined that its complexity necessitated a complete code overhaul and the implementation of new technologies. Front-End and Back-End Overhaul: As part of a comprehensive renewal of the platform, the client was able to redesign the interface to enhance user interaction and aesthetic appeal and upgraded the system to improve performance, scalability, and user-friendliness. Transition to Single-Page Application (SPA): To ensure scalability, we performed a comprehensive assessment of the platform’s needs and determined that its complexity required a complete code rewrite and the adoption of new technologies. These new retail software solutions revolutionized our client’s online fashion platform, enhancing its speed, scalability, and user-friendliness. The partnership showed how maintaining swift and effective communication channels solidify trust and ensure seamless collaboration. Stage 2: Features Extension and Optimization Support and Expertise: Throughout the platform extension phase, the client received robust support and technical expertise, facilitating a seamless and efficient transition as new features were integrated. Additional Functionalities: The client implemented a product ranking automation tool that sorted products by its targeted needs and promoted specific brands. Additionally, it introduced a product information management system to manage all product details. Payment and Shipping: We integrated Klarna as a payment method and configured payments to be country-based, enabling specific payment methods and bonus schemes. We also enabled new shipping options, customizable by country, with new delivery partners. User Experience Enhancement: Our “shop the look” feature allowed customers to purchase entire outfits based on website photos, while integration of a search-as-a-service platform enabled users to filter products by brand, color, and size, significantly improving the shopping experience. The extension and optimization of the platform provided our client with advanced features and tools, greatly enhancing their ecommerce capabilities and elevating user satisfaction. Additionally, the client saw improvements in the look and feel of the website with a new, custom-made UX design, further enhancing the overall user experience. Stage 3: Continuous Improvement To further enhance customer retention, we empowered the client’s SEO expert to implement several key features and significantly boost search engine rankings over an extended period. We also developed and integrated a sophisticated return system that enabled seamless, automated returns directly through the shop. This enhancement streamlined the return process for both customers and the client. Finally, we developed a system allowing customers to create multiple wishlists, integrated with automated emails to improve customer retention and engagement, providing personalized recommendations and updates based on their wishlist activity.

title: Web Summit 2026 travel guide made simple
summary: Plan your Web Summit 2026 trip to Lisbon with per diem data, hotel zone tips, networking frameworks, and a guide from booking to post-conference follow-up.
body_text: Key takeaways Web Summit 2026 brings 70,000+ attendees to Lisbon's Altice Arena from November 9–12, and the trip logistics matter as much as the sessions. Anonymized Navan booking data that reveals when to book, what to budget, and how to avoid the conference-week pricing premium. Hotel prices near Altice Arena increase sharply during Web Summit week, and travelers who book one to two months ahead typically pay about $100 less per night than those who wait until the last minute. Lisbon's conference-week hotel rates often exceed the U.S. State Department lodging per diem, so budget accordingly or consider staying outside Parque das Nações. Lisbon Airport connects to the venue in about 10 minutes via the Metro Red Line, making it one of the easiest conference transfers you'll make. Planning your networking outreach before the conference helps turn a 70,000-person event into a schedule of meaningful meetings. Navan Edge is the personal assistant for business travel that can book flights, hotels, and restaurants in one conversation thread, so you can focus on the conference instead of the logistics. Web Summit 2026 will draw more than 70,000 people from more than 160 countries to Lisbon this November, and the Altice Arena will transform into a four-day crossroads for founders, investors, enterprise leaders, and anyone building or buying technology. The sessions are valuable, but many of the best opportunities happen in hallway conversations and at client dinners. This guide covers the logistics of how to book smart, budget accurately for an international trip, build a realistic conference agenda, and follow up in the most valuble way. What is Web Summit and who is it for? Web Summit is Europe's largest technology conference, hosted annually by Web Summit Ltd. This year, it runs Nov. 9–12, 2026 at Altice Arena (also called MEO Arena) and the Feira Internacional de Lisboa (FIL) exhibition center in Lisbon's Parque das Nações district.[1] The 2026 edition is expected to attract 900-plus speakers, 2,300-plus startups, and 1,200-plus investors from more than 160 countries.[1] General attendee tickets are priced at €1,595, with group discounts available: 10% off for 5–9 tickets 15% off for 10–14 tickets 20% off for 15-plus tickets[1] The crowd spans founders pitching on Centre Stage, investors scanning the startup exhibition, enterprise buyers evaluating SaaS and fintech vendors, developers in specialized tracks, and media covering the week's announcements. If your company sells to technology buyers, raises capital, or partners with startups, a meaningful share of your target market is accessible for four days. November 9 is a pre-conference day featuring badge pickup, mentorship sessions, and opening night. The main conference runs November 10–12, with daily programming from 9 a.m.-5 p.m.[1] Past speakers include Sam Altman (OpenAI), Geoffrey Hinton (University of Toronto), Ursula von der Leyen (European Commission President), Cristiano Amon (Qualcomm CEO), and Alexis Ohanian (Reddit co-founder).[1] Why Web Summit 2026 is worth the trip Web Summit concentrates an unusual density of decision-makers in a four-day window. Your prospect's CTO could be walking the same expo hall. Your integration partner's product lead may be at the same Night Summit event. The investor who passed on your Series A could be attending and open to a conversation over espresso. The conference spans 20-plus content tracks, including dedicated summits for fintech, SaaS, climate tech, marketing, and developer tools.[1] The real value is not only on the main stage. It's in the hallway track, partner dinners, and the conversations that happen after sessions end. Beyond the official agenda, these are some can't-miss happenings: Night Summit , with curated networking events each evening across Lisbon's bars and restaurants Partner-hosted dinners and demo nights in the Chiado, Bairro Alto, and Cais do Sodré neighborhoods 264-plus additional events during Web Summit week, listed on platforms like SideSummit and Luma[2] PITCH competition finals , where early-stage startups present on Centre Stage to global investors Many of the week's best business conversations happen at these side events. The sessions give you context, but the dinners and Night Summit gatherings give you relationships. Plan your trip so you have the energy and calendar space to show up for both. Book your Web Summit flights and hotel early Conference-week hotel prices near Altice Arena climb quickly as Web Summit approaches, making your booking window just as important as your choice of neighborhood. Navan's analysis of hotel bookings from Web Summit 2025 found a median nightly rate of $444 near the venue — roughly 80% higher than a typical October week in Lisbon.[14] Areas in Lisbon with access to Altice Arena Whether you stay within walking distance of the venue or farther away depends on your priorities. Parque das Nações offers the easiest commute, while other neighborhoods can provide lower rates with a short Metro ride. Hotel name Distance to Altice Arena Details Rates Parque das Nações 5-minute walk Flat and modern neighborhood with Vasco da Gama Shopping Centre for essentials Rates are highest during conference week Chiado-Baixa 20 minutes via Metro Access to restaurants, Lisbon's historic center, and direct Red line from Alameda or São Sebastião stations Slightly lower rates than Parque das Nações Avenida da Liberdade 15 minutes via Metro Offers a premium stay outside the conference district, with Metro access via São Sebastião (Red Line) to Oriente High-end hotel options and boutique properties on Lisbon's most elegant boulevard mean higher rates Web Summit hotel pricing and when to book Booking one to two months before check-in offered the best balance of price and availability in Navan's 2025 data. Despite having to pay nearly $100 more per night on average, 40% of conference travelers still booked within two weeks of arrival and 22.9% booked within seven days.[14] Although you can book six or more months out to get your pick of rooms, the rate advantage is less predictable in a smaller sample. Here's when to book based on Navan data from 2025: One to two months out: Median rate of $404, with the best balance of price and availability Two to four weeks out: Median rate of $478, with inventory tightening One to two weeks out: Median rate of $502, as inventory drops Compare any official hotel block against publicly available rates before booking. In some years the conference block offers the best value, but you may find lower prices by booking independently. Flights from the U.S. to Lisbon Lisbon Humberto Delgado Airport (LIS) receives direct flights from several U.S. hubs, including New York/New Jersey (JFK/EWR), Boston, Washington Dulles, and Miami. Flight times range from seven to nine hours, depending on point of origin. For a conference starting Monday, November 9, arriving a day or two early — Saturday, November 7 or Sunday, November 8 — allows time to adjust to the time zone shift before the event begins. How Navan Edge helps with conference travel Navan Edge helps you book flights, hotels, and restaurants in one conversation, backed by AI and 24/7 human travel experts. For Web Summit attendees, Navan Edge lets you compare options across neighborhoods without jumping between booking sites. Triple-dip on hotel stays Navan Edge travelers earn loyalty points from the hotel program, credit card travel rewards, and 5% back in Amazon Gift Cards on eligible hotel stays booked through Navan Edge. On a four-night stay at €200 per night (approximately $870 total), the Amazon Gift Card component amounts to roughly $43 back. Combined, that stacking helps reduce the effective nightly cost . Read Navan Edge's dedicated guide for how to maximize your hotel loyalty points on business trips for a deeper look. Set a realistic Lisbon budget International destinations use per diem rates set by the U.S. State Department rather than domestic General Services Administration (GSA) rates. For Lisbon, the November 2026 allowance is:[4] $350 per day: Includes $249 for lodging and $101 per day for meals and incidental expenses (M&IE) M&IE breakdown: $81 for meals and $20 for incidentals First and last travel days: M&IE drops to 75% of the full rate ($75.75) These rates are effective through December 31, 2026, and can be verified at allowances.state.gov . Budget considerations Now compare that $249 lodging allowance to what Web Summit attendees actually pay. The median nightly rate near Altice Arena during Web Summit 2025 week was $444, a $195-per-night gap between the government allowance and conference-week market rates.[14] Booking one to two months ahead brought the median down to $404, but that still exceeds the per diem cap. If your company reimburses at the State Department rate, you'll likely exceed the reimbursement limit unless you book early or stay in Chiado or Avenida da Liberdade. Be sure to also budget for: Conference ticket: €1,595 (approximately $1,820 USD)[1] Public transportation: Metro from LIS costs €1.90 each way Rideshares and taxis: Uber or Bolt runs €6–10; taxis cost €8–12[5] Daily transit: A daily Viva Viagem pass costs €6.80 and covers Metro, bus, and tram[5] Client dinners: €60–200 per person at Lisbon's business-caliber restaurants After-hours events: Some partner receptions and Night Summit-adjacent dinners carry separate costs beyond the conference ticket Incidentals: Coffee, snacks between sessions, and items you forgot to pack Your $101 daily M&IE allowance goes further in Lisbon than in most U.S. conference cities. A quality lunch near the venue runs €12–18, and a dinner at a locally acclaimed restaurant runs €30–50 per person before drinks. Note: For questions about whether conference travel expenses are tax-deductible, consult a tax professional. Rules vary by jurisdiction and situation. Build your Web Summit agenda in advance Web Summit typically publishes its session catalog several weeks before the conference, and the 1,000-plus speakers across 20-plus tracks creates two common challenges: over-scheduling (eight sessions per day with no gaps) or under-scheduling (winging it and missing the sessions you needed).[1] Most people do best with three to four sessions per day. The Web Summit app is the single most important planning tool. It lets you browse the attendee list, schedule one-on-one meetings, and build a personal agenda before you land in Lisbon.[6] Download it as soon as registration is confirmed. Pre-conference checklist Must-attend keynotes: Centre Stage keynotes set the week's narrative and are recorded, so choose one or two relevant to your role to attend in-person. Workshops and roundtables: These fill fast and are not recorded, making in-person attendance essential. Networking targets: Identify 10–15 specific people you want to meet, send personalized outreach through the app or LinkedIn, and book meetings. Badge pickup: Get your badge on November 9 during the pre-conference period to avoid long queues on the first morning.[6] Book dinner: Confirm meetings with your networking targets and use Navan Edge to book dinner reservations for client meetings before and during Web Summit. Email reminder: Set your out-of-office auto-reply message with return date and emergency contact. Prepare a concise introduction: Be able to explain what you do, why it matters to others, and one specific ask. Cognivix founder Daniele Bernardini, who has attended multiple Web Summits, was quoted on the conference blog, saying, “You should start preparing three months in advance. You should start contacting people, checking who is going to be there … preparation is the best investment of your time, because once you're here, it's too late.”[7] What to wear and pack for Web Summit, Lisbon November highs in Lisbon average 17–19°C (63–66°F) and lows of 11–13°C (52–55°F), with a roughly 24% chance of rain on any given day.[8] The Parque das Nações area, situated along the Tagus River, can feel cooler in the evenings due to waterfront wind. The dress code at Web Summit skews tech-casual, but you should match your audience — not the general crowd. A blazer over a fitted tee works for sessions and most dinners. Enterprise sellers trend slightly more formal, while startup founders trend toward branded hoodies. Web Summit packing list Along with comfortable outfits, we recommend: Two pairs of shoes, including one for dinners and evening events and one for walking, as attendees log 15,000-plus steps daily across venue halls[6] Layers, because temperatures drop after sunset and riverside venues are cooler A waterproof jacket or compact umbrella Chargers for your phone and other devices Noise-canceling earbuds for restful sleep or focus breaks between sessions European power adapter (Type C/F, 230V; U.S. devices need a converter or dual-voltage charger) Snacks, supplements, and vitamins Hand sanitizer and electrolyte packets to stay hydrated and limit germ exposure A passport valid for at least three months beyond your departure date Digital copies of hotel confirmation, conference registration QR code, and transit passes Travel insurance documentation, if necessary Keep your trip documents, hotel confirmations, and flight details accessible in a single chat thread with Navan Edge and eliminate the email-chain scroll when you need your check-in confirmation at the hotel lobby. Your Loyalty Wallet within Navan Edge also stores frequent-flyer and hotel loyalty numbers in one place, simplifying check-in across multiple properties and airlines. Note: U.S. citizens don't need a visa for Portugal. The Schengen area allows stays up to 90 days for tourism and business. Arrival day: Getting from Lisbon Airport to Parque das Nações Lisbon Humberto Delgado Airport (LIS) sits close to the Web Summit venue. The Metro Red Line (Linha Vermelha) runs directly from Aeroporto station to Oriente station (the stop for Parque das Nações) in approximately 10 minutes, at a cost of €1.90 per ride.[5] Trains run every five to eight minutes. Option Duration Cost Best for Metro Red Line (Aeroporto → Oriente) 10 minutes €1.90 Most travelers; fastest and cheapest Uber or Bolt 10–15 minutes €6–10 Heavy luggage, late arrivals Metered taxi 10–15 minutes €8–12 Groups splitting the fare Bus 705 15 minutes €2.30 When Metro is suspended Oriente station is a major transport hub, with direct exits into Vasco da Gama Shopping Centre and the Parque das Nações esplanade.[5] From there, Altice Arena is a five to 10-minute walk along the riverfront. The Web Summit schedule With programming running from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. across Centre Stage, the FIL exhibition halls, and specialized summit tracks, it's important to have a plan. Sessions in Altice Arena and the FIL halls can be a 10-minute walk apart, so build buffer time into your schedule or you'll spend half your day navigating corridors. Consider this agenda: Morning (9–10:30 a.m.): Keynote or one high-priority session, then a scheduled 1:1 meeting over coffee Midday (10:30 a.m.–1 p.m.): Two sessions maximum, with breaks to process and note takeaways Afternoon (1–4 p.m.): Expo floor (startup demos, partner conversations, content track sessions) Evening (5 p.m. onward): One Night Summit event or client dinner Workshops, roundtables, and sessions featuring speakers you want to meet afterward are one of the best uses of your time in person. For the expo floor, head there during Centre Stage keynotes when startup booths are less crowded, rather than immediately after lunch, when foot traffic peaks. If a session conflict means moving your dinner reservation or adding an extra night, Navan Edge handles the change through the same chat where the original booking lives. Indominus Managed Security founder René-Sylvain Bédard, a multi-year attendee, told a reporter for the conference, “You don't actually have time to start learning. You have to go in there and actually know what you want.”[7] Networking that's truly valuable Post-conference connection requests sent within 48 hours outperform those delayed by a week or more, because the conversation is still fresh for both parties. Web Summit networking splits into three phases, and the preparation phase determines the outcome. Before the conference: Build your target list Two weeks before the conference, identify 10–15 specific people to meet with. Look for prospects you've been trying to reach, partners whose product complements yours, and peers in your role at non-competing companies. Use the Web Summit app to browse the attendee list and request 15-minute meetings.[6] A structured pre-event cadence suggests three touchpoints: Day -14 initial outreach Day -7 confirmation Day -1 logistics nudge[9] During the conference: Bring curiosity to the conversation Capture details and context immediately after each conversation: name, company, what you discussed, and what you promised. Here's what to discuss: Ask what brought them to Web Summit this year (identifies their priority) Share one relevant insight from a session or trend you've observed (demonstrates value) Suggest a concrete next step before walking away (“I'll send you that case study by Friday”) After the conference: Follow up within 48 hours Within two days of the conference ending, send personalized LinkedIn connection requests referencing your specific conversation. Deliver on anything you promised, and propose a concrete time to meet again with an agenda. Following this exact pre-event targeting and post-event follow-up system, B2B outreach company hubsell reported generating 18 qualified opportunities from a single Web Summit.[10] Where to eat near Altice Arena during Web Summit There are refreshments provided in the conference venue at Web Summit, but lines grow quickly at peak times.[6] Consider starting the morning with a Portuguese pastel de nata and espresso at a neighborhood café before entering the venue. Bring snacks like protein bars, trail mix, and electrolyte packets to help prevent a 3 p.m. energy drop. For dinners, client meals, and team outings, Lisbon's Parque das Nações district sits along the Tagus River, with direct access to some of the city's strongest dining options, including: Client dinner (building the relationship): Fifty Seconds, a two-Michelin-star restaurant by Chef Rui Silvestre, occupies the top of the Vasco da Gama Tower in Parque das Nações, 120 metres above Lisbon with panoramic views of the Tagus River.[11] The tasting menu runs approximately €200 per person. Book three to four weeks ahead for a window table at sunset. Team or partner meal: Cantinho do Avillez in Parque das Nações, run by celebrated Portuguese chef José Avillez, offers contemporary Portuguese cuisine with river views.[12] Solo recharge or quick meeting: Páteo Restaurante, a traditional Portuguese restaurant in Parque das Nações since 1998, serves specialties in an intimate setting with group menu options available.[13] The Vasco da Gama Shopping Centre food court, steps from Oriente station, provides faster options when time between sessions is limited. During Web Summit, demand at restaurants within walking distance of Altice Arena spikes, and walk-in availability for dinner becomes challenging. Navan Edge can book restaurant reservations through its concierge function. For Web Summit week, booking two to three weeks ahead is prudent: Tell the concierge the purpose of the meal (client dinner for four, Tuesday evening, walking distance from Altice Arena) and let the team handle the search. How to avoid conference burnout at Web Summit Four consecutive days with 15,000-plus steps, dozens of conversations, late-night events, and jet-lag adjustment create compounding fatigue that peaks on the final day. A seven-time Web Summit attendee from FusionAuth summarized the challenge for their company's blog: “Web Summit can be overwhelming. Schedule breaks, hydrate, and take time to relax to avoid burnout. Remember, it's a marathon not a sprint.”[6] A few tips: Take a break: Every three hours, take a break. Walk along the Tagus River waterfront between sessions, return to your hotel for a 20-minute reset if staying in the venue district, or use the time to capture notes from your last conversation while details are fresh. Get some sleep: If you have a 9 a.m. meeting with a prospect, the Night Summit event that runs until midnight costs you the sharpest hours of the following day. Attend one evening event per night maximum. Choose based on who will be there rather than what is being served. Prevent illness: Use hand sanitizer, hydrate beyond what feels necessary, and carry a small bottle of saline nasal spray to combat dry air. If symptoms emerge, skip the evening event and get some extra sleep. Navan Edge's 24/7 human travel experts are available if you need to adjust your booking. For more on what an AI travel agent actually does and how human experts complement the technology, see Navan Edge's guide. Departure day: Late checkout, lounges, and making your flight Most attendees leave Lisbon on November 13, which means hotels in Parque das Nações are busiest around the standard 11 a.m. checkout. If you have a later flight, request a late checkout when you book, or ask the front desk the night before. Hotel loyalty status may include complimentary late checkout, and most properties can store your luggage if you need somewhere to leave it while you squeeze in a final meeting or answer emails. Pack the night before so your departure morning stays focused on wrapping up conversations rather than searching for chargers. When it's time to head to Lisbon Airport, the Metro Red Line from Oriente to Aeroporto is usually the fastest and most reliable option, taking about 10 minutes for €1.65. Rideshare services like Uber and Bolt are convenient, but expect higher prices during the late-morning checkout rush. For international flights, arrive at LIS at least 2 hours before departure to allow time for security and passport control. If you have lounge access through your airline, credit card, or Priority Pass, arriving a little earlier can make the wait far more comfortable. If your plans change, Navan Edge's 24/7 human travel experts can help with late checkout requests or same-day flight changes. After the summit: Re-entry and filing expenses Returning from Lisbon to the U.S. means your body clock is five to eight hours ahead. Plan a light schedule for your first day back. Don't schedule a critical client call for 8 a.m. Eastern on the day you land from a transatlantic flight. Be sure to file your expense report within 48 hours of returning while you still remember which dinner was a client meeting and which rideshare was to an event. Every receipt from Web Summit week involves EUR-to-USD conversion, but you still need to document the exchange rate used for each transaction, which most corporate cards provide automatically. Keep digital copies of all EUR receipts alongside their USD equivalents. Note: Navan Edge is a personal travel booking tool, not an expense management platform. For expense filing and receipt capture, use whatever expense tool your company provides. Make the most of Web Summit 2026 Web Summit moves fast, and the best opportunities often come from the conversations happening between sessions. A little planning before you arrive and disciplined follow-up once you're home can make the difference between a busy week and one that delivers lasting business value. The 3 decisions that matter most: Book your hotel one to two months in advance to secure better rates and availability. Identify 10 people you want to meet and start reaching out about two weeks before the conference. Reserve the 48 hours post-conference to send follow-up messages while conversations are still fresh. title: Enabling Smarter Buildings with PoE, Fiber, and Edge AI
summary: Lantronix | Enabling Smarter Buildings with PoE, Fiber, and Edge AI
body_text: July 27, 2026 General Enabling Smarter Buildings with PoE, Fiber, and Edge AI Buildings are getting smarter and getting smarter fast. Cameras, environmental sensors, wireless access points, lighting systems, HVAC controllers, and digital signage are multiplying across enterprise campuses, healthcare facilities, and commercial properties. With that proliferation comes an urgent operational question: is your network infrastructure actually ready for it? Infrastructure designed five or ten years ago wasn’t built for what’s being asked of it today. The gap between legacy deployments and modern demands is widening and closing it requires more than swapping out a few switches. What’s emerging in response is a convergence of five foundational technology pillars that together form a cohesive platform for next-generation edge infrastructure: Power over Ethernet (PoE) Fiber and Fiber-to-the-Desk Serial-to-Ethernet connectivity Out-of-Band Management Edge AI Modern edge networks must simultaneously deliver power, carry greater bandwidth, and surface actionable intelligence. Architectures that address only one or two of those dimensions will leave critical gaps. PoE: Powering the Next Generation of Smart Devices Power over Ethernet has been around for years, but its latest generation unlocks capabilities that simply weren’t possible before. At its core, PoE delivers both power and data over a single Ethernet cable thereby eliminating the need for separate electrical infrastructure at every endpoint. The standard has evolved significantly across three generations: Standard Max Power Typical Use Cases IEEE 802.3af 15W IP phones, basic cameras PoE+ (802.3at) 30W PTZ cameras, wireless access points PoE++ (802.3bt) 60–90W LED lighting, digital signage, thin clients That top-end PoE++ capability is particularly significant for intelligent LED lighting. PoE-powered luminaires enable per-fixture dimming, occupancy-based automation, and real-time energy metering. The reported energy reductions of 50 to 70 percent across deployments, which for large commercial buildings, that’s a material impact on operating costs. Beyond lighting, PoE serves as the connectivity backbone for smart building IoT: access control, environmental sensors, digital signage, and industrial devices. Because all endpoints are powered through the switch, remote power cycling is straightforward which dramatically simplifies day-to-day operations. When PoE switches are backed by UPS or generator power, every connected device stays online during a grid outage, keeping security systems and building automation running continuously. Fiber: The Foundation of Future-Ready Networks Copper has served enterprise networking well, but it carries inherent constraints including a 100-meter distance limit and a hard bandwidth ceiling. As buildings scale and workloads intensify, those constraints become real bottlenecks. Fiber eliminates them. It supports 10GbE and 25GbE connections, spans distances measured in kilometers rather than meters and is completely immune to electromagnetic interference. This is a significant advantage in environments with heavy industrial equipment or dense RF activity. Two fiber benefits that often go underappreciated are security and sustainability . Unlike copper, fiber doesn’t radiate electromagnetic signals, which matters for government, finance, and healthcare environments where signal leakage is a compliance concern. Physical tampering is also immediately detectable as a measurable drop in light transmission. On the sustainability side, fiber’s dramatically longer lifecycle means bandwidth upgrades happen at the transceiver, not the cable which fundamentally changes the economics of infrastructure refresh cycles. Fiber-to-the-Desk takes these advantages all the way to the endpoint with secure, high-bandwidth, interference-free connectivity at the workstation level, ideal for secure facilities, dense office environments, and air-gapped network requirements. Serial-to-Ethernet: Bridging Legacy into Modern IP Networks Look inside any industrial facility, hospital, or older commercial building, and you’ll find serial interfaces everywhere: RS-232, RS-485, RS-422 from PLCs, HVAC controllers, point-of-sale systems, access control panels, medical devices, console ports. These devices represent significant capital investment and are often deeply embedded in operations. Serial device servers solve the integration challenge through transparent protocol conversion where the serial device believes it’s communicating with another serial device, while the network sees standard TCP/IP traffic. The integration is seamless, and the existing equipment stays in service. Serial interfaces persist for good reason: they’re deterministic, simple, and purpose-built, with no IP configuration to manage, no DHCP dependency, and have minimal firmware attack surface. That simplicity is a feature in machine-interface contexts. Serial device servers modernize that infrastructure without replacing it, extending its useful life while enabling centralized remote access, logging, and monitoring across every connected device. Out-of-Band Management: Network Resilience When It Matters Most Every network team has experienced some version of this scenario: a critical device becomes unreachable. You attempt to log in and diagnose the problem but the management path runs over the same network that just failed. You’re locked out of the tools you need to fix the outage. This is the fundamental circular dependency of in-band management. Out-of-Band Management (OOB) breaks that dependency by establishing a dedicated management plane that is physically separate from the production network . Typically the connection is via an independent cellular LTE or 5G path. When the primary network fails, management access remains available regardless of what’s happening on the production side. The operational impact is measurable. Without OOB, an outage typically requires a field dispatch meaning response times measured in hours . With OOB, remote and often autonomous diagnosis and remediation bring that down to minutes . For multi-site organizations in retail, healthcare, or financial services, the ROI is compelling because the cost of a single prevented field dispatch can justify the investment across an entire site. Edge AI: Intelligence Where Data Is Born The traditional model sends data to the cloud for processing. As data volumes have grown, the problems with that model have become harder to ignore including cloud latency, WAN bandwidth consumption, cloud dependency risk, and maybe most critically, sensitive operational data leaving the organizational perimeter. Edge AI inverts this model. Intelligence runs at the point where data is generated, eliminating those constraints entirely. In practice, that looks like: Device health monitoring | ML models detect anomalous telemetry and predict hardware failure before it happens. Traffic anomaly detection | Flags intrusion, malware, or DDoS in real time, faster than signature-based approaches. Predictive capacity management | Forecasts bandwidth saturation before users experience it. Root cause analysis | Correlates symptoms across devices and identifies problem sources in seconds rather than hours. Dynamic energy optimization | Adjusts PoE power budgets based on actual consumption patterns across the building. The optimal insertion point for edge AI is the fiber aggregation layer. By embedding intelligence at aggregation, organizations gain visibility across their entire existing switching and IP device infrastructure without replacing cameras, sensors, or access points with purpose-built AI hardware. That means time-to-value measured in weeks, not years. A Practical Path Forward: Three Phases Moving from where most organizations are today to a fully intelligent edge network doesn’t require a rip-and-replace approach. A phased rollout lets teams build incrementally while delivering value at each stage. Phase 1 – Foundation Assess existing copper for PoE capability, identify fiber upgrade candidates, and deploy Out-of-Band management for critical devices. This delivers immediate resilience improvements with modest investment and is where most organizations can start today. Phase 2 – Modernization Extend PoE to smart building endpoints, roll out Fiber-to-the-Desk for security systems and high-bandwidth workstations, and deploy serial device servers for priority legacy equipment. This phase expands capability and builds the data foundation that edge AI will use. Phase 3 – Intelligence Deploy edge AI integrated across PoE infrastructure, network monitoring, and serial device telemetry. At this stage, infrastructure transitions from a passive transport layer to an active, self-monitoring system that predicts problems and automates responses. Each phase is sequential by design: each one builds the data foundation the next relies on. But they can be paced to match budget cycles and operational priorities, making the investment manageable even for organizations with constrained capex. Ready to Get Started? Whether you’re a reseller partner or evaluating edge infrastructure for your own organization, Lantronix offers a complete, integrated solution stack spanning PoE switching, fiber, serial device servers, Out-of-Band management, and edge AI — all managed through a single platform. title: The Future of Manufacturing Tax: Preparing for What's Next
summary: Vertex is the leading and most-trusted provider of comprehensive, integrated tax technology solutions, having helped 10,000+ businesses since 1978.
body_text: Share Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Linkedin Share via Email When manufacturing experts peer into their crystal ball, they see a future defined by cross-industry collaboration, connected products, and integrated solutions. When indirect tax leaders consider these “Manufacturing 2030” trends, they’re likely to see an imposing set of tax compliance challenges. Based on surveys of more than 400 industrial manufacturing leaders around the world, PwC’s 2026 global manufacturing outlook assesses trends, opportunities, and risks in the sector while focusing on the most notable ways manufacturing executives expect their organizations to evolve during the next four years. Key takeaways from the report include: Technology enablement and automation adoption are surging throughout supply chains. Survey respondents expect supply chains to be two to three times more automated than they are in 2026. By 2030, competitive advantage will stem less from having advanced tools in place than from how well the tools and data they use are orchestrated. Revenue growth will come from sources other than traditional industrial and consumer products . This translates to more product-service bundles, connected offerings, and outcome-based services. Upskilling and digital/data infrastructure are at risk . The survey report warns that underinvesting in both areas will make it difficult for manufacturing companies to take full advantage of growth opportunities. New enablers are emerging : Manufacturers will outperform competitors on the basis of operational excellence, customer-centricity, and innovation – and that the execution of these strategies requires “clean, connected data; interoperable systems; disciplined operating models; and strong, trust-based organizational cultures,” as per the report. Manufacturing Tax Challenges Through 2030 A couple of these trends will raise eyebrows across indirect tax groups. Regarding changing sources of growth, the report indicates that 44% of total revenue is projected to come from outside the manufacturing of industrial and consumer products by 2030 via: Technology, digital, and communications products and services Defense, governmental, and educational offerings Energy and fuel production and distribution How Tax Can Keep Pace As manufacturers move into new categories, collaborate with new partners, and create new products, larger numbers of new SKUs will need to be classified for VAT/GST and sales and use tax (SUT) purposes. Exemption management processes will also need to keep pace with these changes. New offerings related to energy and fuel distribution can push traditional manufacturers beyond their existing compliance footprints into excise-tax and environmental-levy regimes. Another tax compliance challenges looms. As manufacturers develop and sell larger volumes of integrated solutions (as opposed to discrete products), those offerings will need to be parsed from multiple tax angles. Bundling is thorny from an indirect tax compliance perspective. Is the offering composite or mixed? Does a single rate apply or do multiple rates come into play? Are there any exempt elements? Answers to those and other questions vary by tax jurisdiction. Outcome - and subscription-based models also change the timing and nature of taxable transactions: one-time sales give way to recurring supplies that require ongoing invoicing, time-of-supply determinations, and – in some tax regimes – continuous reporting. The report emphasizes that data integrity will be a foundational pillar of the emerging environment, which PwC describes as a “race to tech-enable and automate broad swaths of industrial manufacturing.” A similar idea applies to indirect tax: tax data integrity , supported by a purpose-built tax engine, must be a foundational enabler of an advanced tax compliance and planning capability if tax groups are to keep pace in the race to 2030. This Vertex-BDO white paper is a good starting point; it details how leading manufacturers are leveraging automation to address tax compliance today. He is responsible for providing insights, thought leadership and customer-centric direction to Vertex functional groups, supporting the continued expansion of Vertex indirect tax solutions and overall enterprise strategy. He has over 35 years of experience in sales, use, and VAT tax compliance, risk assessment, jurisdictional audits, administration and management. Larry joined Vertex in 2005 as a Sales and Income Tax Supervisor and then as Tax Manager in 2012, where he played a pivotal role in elevating and advancing the company’s tax management offerings.

title: The Value of Sustainability
body_text: What Mercer’s 2025 Sustainability Days Mean for Our Day-to-Day Work At Mercer, sustainability is neither an abstract concept nor a topic reserved for management or reports. It directly shapes our daily work – how we produce, invest, and future-proof our sites. This was precisely the focus of the second annual 2025 Mercer Sustainability Days. Under the guiding theme, “The Value of Sustainability,” one key question took center stage: How do our projects at the mills help secure jobs, remain competitive, and use resources responsibly? Sustainability is not an add-on, but an integral part of how Mercer operates as a company – at every site. Climate Protection as a Strategic Competitive Advantage One of the key takeaways from the German Sustainability Days was unmistakable: tackling climate change is no longer optional, but a strategic necessity to safeguard our competitiveness with European and global customers. Customers expect quantifiable improvements in the emissions intensity of our products to meet their own ambitious sustainability targets. Our Pre-evaporator project at Mercer Rosenthal is a prime example of how we meet these expectations. An evaporator is a large process equipment that boils off water from a liquid so what’s left becomes more concentrated. At a pulp mill, evaporators are used to remove water from the “black liquor” that comes out of the pulping process. That concentrated liquor is then sent to the recovery system, where it helps the mill recover chemicals and generate energy. A pre-evaporator is simply an extra “first step” evaporator added ahead of the main evaporators. It uses recovered, low-value heat to remove some water early, which reduces the mill’s need for fresh steam and water and can free up steam to make more electricity. Specifically, we reduce raw water intake by 22 cubic meters per hour – more than 500 cubic meters per day – while also saving chemicals. Through the consistent recovery of steam and water, we are significantly reducing our resource consumption while increasing our internal power generation by 0.97 MW – equivalent to the average annual electricity demand of around 2,000 households. A process improvement thus becomes a profit center. This is exactly what we mean when we say: sustainability is good business. Every cubic meter of water saved and every kilowatt generated internally strengthens our operational and financial resilience. The conversion of the lime kiln to biomass at the Mercer Stendal mill is a strategic investment with the clear goal of significantly reducing our Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions. A lime kiln in a pulp mill is necessary for the process of recovering cooking chemicals so that they can be reused in production. The conversion to biomass means that fossil fuels (natural gas) are replaced by bio-based, renewable fuels to generate the heat for the lime burning process. This reduces fossil CO₂ emissions, decreases dependence on fossil fuels, and utilizes local by-products that would otherwise remain unused. Mercer is firmly committed to this project, as it is central to our position as a preferred supplier. Leading European customers no longer view reducing emissions along the supply chain as a desire, but as a prerequisite for a long-term partnership. The example of Mercer Stendal clearly shows that with a bold climate investment, we are directly contributing to our sustainable business success and our future viability. Efficiency in Action: How Our Mills Save Resources and Become More Profitable The results from our North American mills vividly show that sustainability and economic performance go hand in hand. At the Mercer Celgar mill , fiber losses have been reduced by 57% since 2022 . More than half of the fibers that used to be lost now remain in the production cycle. Previously, losses in the Reverse Centrifugal Cleaners (RCC) area of the pulp machine room amounted to approximately 4.2 air-dry metric tons (ADMT) per day. At the same time, lime waste sent to landfills has been reduced by one third, resulting in tangible savings in disposal and operating costs. At the Mercer Peace River mill, the 4DX program (Four Disciplines of Execution). It’s a practical method MPR is using to make sure important goals do not get lost in day-to-day work: MPR will pick a small number of top priorities, measure the actions that drive results, and use a simple scoreboard so everyone can see progress. 4DX demonstrates how safety, planning, and efficiency reinforce each other. Increased planned maintenance shutdowns significantly reduced unplanned outages. Equipment now runs more reliably, consumes less natural gas, and incurs lower costs. These results are not abstract metrics – they directly strengthen the operational resilience of our mills. Another forward-looking project at Mercer Peace River investigates the pelletization of landfill waste to be used in agricultural beneficial re-use applications which can improve soil health by raising pH levels. The collaboration with a liming plant has the potential capacity to use up to 50,000 tons of landfilled materials annually.. This corresponds to the weight of around 25,000 mid-range cars that would no longer end up in landfills. The Power of Wood: Mass Timber and the Future of Carbon Storage The Mass Timber Sustainability Day highlighted the unique role of engineered wood products such as cross-laminated timber (CLT) and glue-laminated timber (GL). Wood products can store biogenic carbon for decades while in service, and can support lower-carbon construction when used in place of more emissions-intensive materials. We have already realized this potential in large-scale projects. A well-known example is Google’s YouTube headquarters, a building constructed using Mercer’s mass timber. Projects like this demonstrate that sustainable construction and economic success go hand in hand. Mass timber is a key growth area for Mercer. Our strong market position is demonstrated by our collaboration with Google: together, we completed the Google 1265 Borregas project last year. The five-story office building covers 182,500 square meters and sets new standards for sustainable design with its solid wood construction. Every additional wooden building means less CO₂ in the atmosphere and more carbon stored in durable products. By 2030, our goal is to increase the long-term carbon storage from mass timber by 200% from 2024 by increasing our production. Responsible forestry is the basis of our actions. Mercer will support five Principles for Responsible Timber Construction developed by the Built by Nature organization. These principles focus on extending building life, whole-life-cycle impacts, sustainable forest management, maximizing carbon storage, and supporting a timber building bioeconomy. Decarbonization and Efficiency as Keys to Competitiveness The Sustainability Days at Mercer Holz, Mercer Timber Products , and Mercer Torgau clearly showed where the greatest levers lie for our German sites: consistent decarbonization and increased operational efficiency. Both are essential to securing our competitiveness in our global markets. At Mercer Holz , the focus was particularly on logistics, as transportation is one of the largest drivers of fossil energy consumption. A key success is the LoOP ( lo gistic op timization) project for digital truck processing. At the Rosenthal, Friesau, Torgau, and Stendal sites, up to 700 trucks are processed digitally every day. Freight forwarders can now use our logistics portal to independently register their trucks and drivers and plan time slots flexibly. The app lets drivers book time slots and electronically transmit relevant information, including delivery bills. The result: a paperless process, shorter waiting times, and more efficient operations that save more than €400,000 annually and avoid 183 tonnes of CO₂ by reducing truck idling. Complementing this, the E-truck project was presented, with two fully electric trucks now in operation. They demonstrate significant potential: energy consumption is approximately two and a half times lower compared to conventional diesel trucks. This is supported by the terminal strategy, which shifts long-distance timber transport to rail. From a distance of around 70 kilometers, rail transport is significantly more CO₂-efficient than road transport. At Mercer Timber Products , the focus was on optimizing load monitoring for railcars. By reducing underloading, €202,000 in costs had already been saved by August 2025. At the same time, improved utilization results in annual CO₂ savings of around 60 tonnes – a clear example of how operational precision delivers direct economic and environmental benefits. Mercer Torgau makes a central contribution to group-wide decarbonization. The site supplies the Stendal pulp mill with residual wood chips and is planned to provide pellets in the future to support the decarbonization of the lime kiln at Stendal by replacing natural gas. With an annual pellet production capacity of around 140,000 tonnes, up to approximately 80,000 tonnes of Torgau’s pellets could be used for this purpose. At the same time, Mercer Torgau will continue to produce and market pellets for external customers. In parallel, Mercer Torgau is strategically shifting its production toward higher-value structural timber. The goal is to reduce dependence on the currently weak demand for industrial pallets and to increase the overall resilience of the business model. Outlook This year’s Sustainability Days once again demonstrated that sustainability at Mercer is not a separate topic, but an integral part of our business – driving efficiency, innovation, and competitiveness. From the strategic necessity of climate protection to concrete efficiency projects and the future of the bioeconomy, our commitment creates value at every level. Each of these projects began with an idea – the value of sustainability is evident in the details. That’s why we will be highlighting each of our key projects individually over the coming months. We will provide you with exclusive background information and show you how we are making our locations future-proof, step by step. Don’t miss a single post in our new series – coming soon to our blog!

title: Predictive coding announcement

body_text: Routable’s newest AI innovation expands on invoice automation to predict bill codes, saving time for accounts payable teams New AI features make manual bill coding a thing of the past ATLANTA, GA. June 9 , 2025. Routable , the leading accounts payable automation platform, announced its newest AI features today at the Sage Future conference in Atlanta: predictive bill coding. This feature expands on Routable’s robust invoice automation solutions for an end-to-end invoice processing experience. “The promise of OCR has long been unfulfilled, leaving finance and accounting professionals feeling discouraged. With the latest advances in AI and machine learning, Routable is able to not only deliver on that promise, but also take it further,” said Omri Mor, CEO and Co-founder of Routable. “Predictive coding revolutionizes how AP teams process bills, shifting the work from manual data entry to review for a near touchless experience.” Routable’s Purchase Order (PO) matching solution already inherits PO codes for a touchless invoice coding process. For non-PO backed invoices, Routable will now leverage machine learning to predict codes for the invoice, even at the line item level. Accounts Payable professionals simply upload an invoice, check that codes are accurate, and save the bill. If any coding is incorrect, the AP team can make corrections, and the system will learn from those adjustments to improve future predictions. Additionally, if the OCR misreads any invoice details, the team can retrain it, helping the system become more accurate over time. Predictive coding is just the latest AI-powered innovation from Routable. Routable previously announced invoice fraud prevention , which uses machine learning and generative AI to detect invoice fraud. “As we move into a new era of work, I’m constantly looking for partners who think ahead,” commented Brandt Kucharski, CAO at Ethos. “Routable continuously pushes the innovation envelope, and the newest AI features are no exception. Predictive coding picks up where OCR leaves off, for a fully automated invoice capture and processing experience.” About Routable Routable’s Accounts Payable Automation platform offers the most efficient and robust solution to streamline and scale the end-to-end AP process. With automated invoice capture and processing, flexible payment options, and seamless vendor management, Routable reduces manual payment tasks by 80% so finance teams can focus on impact. Routable’s deep ERP integrations and configurable approval workflows support complex business requirements with ease. Routable eliminates compliance headaches through detailed audit trails, role-based access, and vendor risk checks. All with an average savings of 30%. AP Automation, solved.

title: BellRing Brands Appoints Michael Axelrod as Chief Executive Officer
summary: BellRing Brands Appoints Michael Axelrod as Chief Executive Officer
body_text: ST. LOUIS, July 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BellRing Brands, Inc. (NYSE:BRBR) (“BellRing”) today announced that Michael Axelrod has been appointed as the company’s next President and Chief Executive Officer, effective July 29, 2026. He will also be appointed to the Company’s Board of Directors. Darcy Davenport, who announced her intention to retire from the Company earlier this year, will serve in a senior advisory capacity to support a seamless leadership transition and provide strategic support. Mr. Axelrod is an accomplished executive with more than 30 years of experience in the consumer packaged goods industry, including serving as CEO of several consumer companies. He has a demonstrated track record of driving profitable growth, leading business transformation and creating long-term shareholder value across both entrepreneurial and large-scale consumer businesses. Throughout his career, he has built strong customer partnerships, accelerated innovation, improved operational performance and built high-performing teams. He joins BellRing from Snak King, a leading manufacturer of salty snacks, where he served as CEO. He was previously the CEO of Del Real Foods where he oversaw significant revenue growth, national expansion and operational improvements. Earlier in his career, he held senior leadership roles at Passport Food Group, TreeHouse Foods and Kraft Foods. Prior to his operating leadership roles, he began his career at Boston Consulting Group, where he advised consumer and retail clients. “We conducted an extensive search and determined that Mike is uniquely qualified to lead BellRing. His record of strategic insight, strong customer relationships and operational excellence will be invaluable as we embark on the next chapter of growth,” said Robert V. Vitale, Chairman of the Board of Directors. “On behalf of the Board of Directors, I want to thank Darcy for her many years of dedicated service to BellRing through a significant period of growth to over $2.3 billion in sales. We are grateful for her leadership, her many contributions to BellRing, and her partnership in ensuring a successful transition.” “I am honored to be chosen as the next leader of BellRing,” said Mike Axelrod. “Consumer demand for protein remains exceptionally strong. With the #1 ready-to-drink protein brand, deep category expertise and strong retailer relationships, BellRing is well positioned to drive long-term growth through customer focus, innovation and operational rigor. I look forward to partnering with the Board and the team to capitalize on the significant opportunities ahead, further strengthen our market position and deliver long-term value for stakeholders.” About Michael Axelrod Michael Axelrod most recently served as CEO of Snak King, a leading manufacturer of branded and private label salty snacks. He was previously the CEO of Del Real Foods, where he oversaw significant revenue growth, national expansion and operational improvements. Prior to Del Real Foods, he spent two years as CEO of Passport Food Group and five years at TreeHouse Foods as President, Condiments Division and Chief Operating Officer, Bay Valley Foods. Earlier in his career he held executive roles at Whirlpool Corporation, Kraft Foods, McCain Foods and Pactiv Corporation (acquired by Reynolds Consumer Products). He began his career at Boston Consulting Group leading strategy engagements for consumer and retail clients. He holds an honors bachelor’s degree from the University of Western Ontario Ivey Business School and a Master of Business Administration from the Northwestern University Kellogg School of Management.
